rdme-hierarchical-transfer.problem: Track spurs are dense at seeding and then dilute, but the RDME can only coarsen the whole grid once the dispersion test passes everywhere, so isolated spurs keep the full grid fine.
rdme-hierarchical-transfer.solution: hRDME (Hellander & Hellander 2020): molecules start on the finest admissible mesh and move up one level after diffusing for t_transfer = C h^2/(6D) (C = 1 to 20); reported speed-ups are 400-2000x. radkin uses the count-based next-subvolume method without per-molecule ages, so it would need age cohorts per species and voxel, or a next-particle variant. Depends on rdme-multigrid-species. Research-grade.
rdme-hierarchical-transfer.benefits: Local, age-driven coarsening matched to spur dilution.
rdme-hierarchical-transfer.sourceDirection: read '_lite.md' version of scientific papers in 'radkin\docs\literature\md_mistral\'. How could these papers benefit radkin repo?

crdme-neighbour-reactions.problem: Below h* no local rate makes the RDME correct (Hellander 2012), yet radiolysis spurs call for nm voxels, and one bundled reaction has h* = 75 nm.
crdme-neighbour-reactions.solution: Convergent RDME (Isaacson & Zhang 2018): discretise the Doi model so that A in V_i and B in V_j react with kappa_ij = lambda |overlap within eps| / (|V_i||V_j|), and products are placed by kappa_k|ij. On radkin's uniform Cartesian grid kappa depends only on the voxel offset, so it is a precomputed stencil. It needs a Doi radius and rate per reaction (derived from k and D) and a rework of the per-voxel propensity bookkeeping. Large; only after rdme-mesh-corrected-rates shows where the local correction runs out.
crdme-neighbour-reactions.benefits: Converges as h goes to 0; the only route to valid sub-h* voxels.

ssa-cdme-derivation-note.problem: docs/ssa.md justifies the 2A propensity k n(n-1)/(N_A V) and the hop rules numerically (the factor-2 experiment) but not from a common particle-level model.
ssa-cdme-derivation-note.solution: Add a short derivation section citing the chemical diffusion master equation (del Razo et al. 2023), which gives the combinatorial factors for decay, binding and annihilation and the CME and RDME as its limits. Documentation only; no code change.
ssa-cdme-derivation-note.benefits: A traceable theoretical basis for the propensity conventions.
